tasks.short: Teach acceptable behavior through responsive reinforcement

steps.what: Teach socially acceptable behavior through modelling, practice, behavior modification and positive reinforcement during actual pupil interactions

tasks.design: Keep the teacher present for modelling, practice and reinforcement. A {LMS} activity library cannot replace contingent responses to an actual pupil, and this task establishes no separate record or send to automate.
tasks.previous_blocker: The response depends on the pupil and immediate classroom situation.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable materials exist, but do not remove the teacher's responsive instruction.
tasks.still_hard: Choose a proportionate response without misreading the pupil's communication.

ambition.what: No additional capacity claimed from this change.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: behavior teaching requires contextual teacher responses; a material library is not a replacement for that interaction.

assumptions: Boundary is actual teaching and reinforcement, using an already agreed support approach. The statement does not establish a separate report, record write, lookup or send; none is assigned invented baseline time.
No new structured input, software or capture is required. Native lesson resources were considered but do not change this live step.
The 100% share denotes the whole task boundary, not measured duration. Zero upkeep follows from making no software change.
unknowns: Whether the local task also includes a separately timed behavior log; if present it must be decomposed and measured.
research_questions: Observe an actual session and identify any record work performed during the instruction.

incremental.description: No new tool, recording or rule maintenance introduced

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Live reinforcement remains wholly human; no separate documented administrative work has been established.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Adapt curriculum materials to a pupil's learning needs

steps.what: Read the general education curriculum and the pupil's existing learning goals and access requirements
inputs: existing pupil learning goals and access requirements

steps.what: Choose which objectives to preserve and which instructional techniques and technologies suit this pupil
outputs: teacher's adaptation instructions and preserved objectives

steps.what: Rewrite activities, explanations and response formats to the selected objectives and access requirements
inputs: teacher's adaptation instructions and preserved objectives
outputs: adapted curriculum draft with source links

loop.purpose: Draft alternate explanations and activity formats
loop.input: Teacher-selected curriculum passages, objectives and adaptation instructions
loop.output: Adapted draft with objective and source references
loop.check: Teacher checks meaning, preserved learning demand, accessibility and suitability; no diagnostic claims or new pupil assessments
loop.stop: At most two drafts; teacher rewrites unsupported or unsuitable parts
loop.why_not_simpler: Native copying and templates cannot rewrite instructional meaning to a specific access requirement

steps.what: Test the completed adaptation's instructions, accessible presentation and instructional suitability and select the final curriculum version
inputs: adapted curriculum draft with source links

steps.what: Save the selected final curriculum version in the same lesson system

tasks.design: Test the {LMS} editor's native adaptation functions first, using only teacher-selected curriculum and requirements. A bounded rewrite produces a draft, while the teacher selects objectives, checks the completed material and saves that exact version in {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Different access needs require different explanations and response formats.
tasks.enabler_now: An editor can draft variants from supplied text without taking over curriculum decisions.
tasks.still_hard: An easier text may unintentionally remove the intended concept or learning demand.
tasks.human_edge: Know how a particular pupil learns and verify the adaptation in practice.

ambition.what: Prepare an additional accessible response format for pupils unable to use the standard worksheet.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: lesson editors can support text adaptation; teachers must check learning meaning and pupil suitability.

assumptions: Boundary is curriculum modification, not live instruction, grading or a change to pupil placement. OPS_SYSTEM denotes the school pupil-record system.

The curriculum owner supplies versioned source material; the teacher selects existing goal identifiers, relevant access requirements and adaptation instructions. If records cannot be accessed, teacher selects passages manually; no uncounted extraction or new student assessment is assumed.
Shares are an unmeasured task-specific scenario, independent of prompt priors. Drafting is actual modification work; no new preparation report or formal approval meeting is invented.

Native editing is tested first. The 1% same-system save is fully retained and earns no saving. Final selection in s4 is the teacher's existing suitability decision after the full material exists; later edits require another check.
Gross saving is 18 hours per 100 baseline hours; 1 incremental hour leaves 17 net. Review in s3 and s4 is already counted.
unknowns: Actual drafting share and native editor support
School's permitted pupil-data processing and access
research_questions: Can teachers preserve objective meaning while reducing drafting effort on actual curriculum adaptations?

already_counted.description: Draft correction and completed-material suitability check

incremental.description: Maintain adaptation instructions and review recurring editor failures

approvals.approved_version: teacher-selected final curriculum version from s4, invalidated by any edit

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if the editor cannot produce suitable formats; up to 14% if writing dominates but correction takes longer than the central 17% net scenario.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Apply specialist instructional techniques during teaching

steps.what: Employ special educational strategies during instruction and adapt sensory, perceptual-motor, language, cognition and memory activities to the pupil's response
outputs: supported practice using suitable special educational techniques

tasks.design: Keep the teacher responsible for special educational techniques during actual instruction. {LMS} material preparation can change a different task, but supplies no demonstrated reduction in this live response work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Methods must be adjusted to an individual pupil's actual response.
tasks.enabler_now: Instructional technologies offer practice formats without replacing specialist attention.
tasks.still_hard: Judge whether a response reflects understanding, an access barrier or fatigue.
tasks.human_edge: Observe carefully and change the activity without imposing an inferred diagnosis.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: using special educational techniques during instruction depends on teacher observation and adjustment.

assumptions: The boundary is the statement's application of techniques during instruction. It specifies no separate written assessment, record or send. No administrative baseline is invented.
No new structured record is required; inputs are the actual activity and pupil response. Native resources do not reduce the live teaching step.
No change means no incremental upkeep. The single share describes this task boundary rather than an observed time allocation.
unknowns: Whether local observation recording is performed as a distinct part of this task
research_questions: Observe the task to separate any actual written observation from live instructional adjustment.

incremental.description: No introduced software or recording work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Specialist instruction stays fully retained; no separate record-writing work is established by this statement.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer on pupils' behavioral and academic problems

steps.what: Consult existing learning and behavior records relevant to the pupil problem before discussion
inputs: existing teacher observations and learning records

steps.what: Confer with parents or guardians, teachers, counselors and administrators to understand and resolve the pupil's behavioral and academic problems
outputs: discussed causes, support choices and agreed next actions

tasks.design: Configure the native pupil view in {OPS_SYSTEM} to show the relevant existing learning and behavior entries together. The teacher checks those facts and conducts the discussion with the family and school colleagues; no generated diagnosis or new follow-up report is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant existing observations may sit in different pupil-record views.
tasks.enabler_now: Native filtered views can reduce navigation while preserving source entries.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve differing accounts and agree support acceptable to the pupil and family.
tasks.human_edge: Listen to concerns and use contextual knowledge without treating records as the whole story.

ambition.what: A small navigation change does not establish capacity for additional conferences.

build_days.consent_and_access: 1-4; permitted pupil-record views and applicable consultation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: pupil-record views can gather existing entries, but resolving behavioral and academic problems remains a human discussion.

assumptions: Boundary includes consultation of existing facts and the actual conference. The statement establishes no separate minutes, new report or outbound message; do not add one merely to create savings.

OPS_SYSTEM is the school pupil-record system. Existing observations are authored by the teachers who observed them; inputs are pupil ID, dated observation text and learning record. Missing entries are discussed as unknown, not generated or retrospectively captured for free.
A 5% lookup share and 20% lookup reduction are provisional scenarios, not measured baselines. Test native views first; no change is warranted if facts are already available in one view.
Gross saving 1 hour per 100; view upkeep 0.2 leaves 0.8 net. Discussion includes live agreement, not a fabricated document approval.
unknowns: Actual navigation burden and whether relevant records already share one view
research_questions: Does a native view save navigation time without hiding contradictory observations?

already_counted.description: Check the existing entries selected for discussion

incremental.description: Review view filters when record categories change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Zero if the existing view already suffices; up to 0.5% net where navigation shrinks less than the provisional central 0.8% net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher retains pupil-facing instruction and support decisions; curriculum drafting receives limited assistance.
reach: Help an instructional coordinator review accessible curriculum formats
skills_to_grow: Check adapted material against learning objectives
Use native pupil-record views without inferring unsupported conclusions
role.ambitious_version: Provide additional accessible activity formats while keeping specialist teaching and family discussions with the teacher.
